pushback_verification: All 13 verified against the built tree before any edit; ZERO stale. Six were reproduced empirically rather than reasoned about, each with a runnable case: the nested-fence ruling miscount (returned 2, correct answer 1), the schema traversal (emitted 777 from outside both tiers), the prototype key (raw TypeError, not the clean error), the compact-comment marker parsing live, the empty sources map yielding a silent present-but-inert registry, and the escaped-backtick mask swallowing a marker.

resolutions.title: The modified opacity contract is false of the existing parser API
resolutions.action: DEFERRED by explicit user ratification. Verified real before deferring: ParsedArchitectureDoc.lines is a public field carrying the whole document, sliceStageSection reads it downstream for `architecture show`, and countRulingEntries obtains the rulings THROUGH that same field — so the delta's 'nothing downstream of parseArchitectureDoc may read it' and its single-named-exception claim are both false of the shipped API. Not repaired here: the fix is either separating raw bytes from the parsed model or rewriting the requirement around what 'reads' means and naming every permitted reader, which is a spec REDESIGN and routes back to explore under R-crc-6 rather than being invented inside a walk.
resolutions.resolution: Intentionally defer external C1; walk the remaining list.

resolutions.title: The ruling source counts entries inside valid fenced code
resolutions.action: Applied option A: countRulingEntries now builds its line mask from the SHARED createFenceTracker (new fenceMaskFor helper) instead of the requirement-block depth heuristic. Reproduced the defect first — a four-backtick fence around a three-backtick example returned 2 where the answer is 1, admitting both fenced bullets and masking the live one — and confirmed it returns 1 after the fix while the live R-crc count stays 10. Two regressions added (nested fence; three-backtick line cannot close a four-backtick fence).
resolutions.resolution: Option A (contained fix) settled under R-crc-3 and applied under the user's blanket directive; migrating the architecture PARSER off the heuristic is recorded in design.md D3 as a declared residual with kind and method, because it is engine-wide grammar unification consumed by status/show/validate and inventing it inside a walk is what R-crc-6 forbids.

options_presented.label: A
options_presented.body: change only countRulingEntries to use the shared tracker

options_presented.label: B
options_presented.body: also migrate architecture/parser.ts so the engine has one fence grammar

resolutions.title: Marker recognition accepts comments outside the specified exact grammar
resolutions.action: Tightened OPENER_REGEX/CLOSER_REGEX to the exact literal delimiters (one space, NAME the only pattern). Verified the compact form parsed live before the fix. Four inertness regressions added: compact, tabbed, double-spaced, split-across-lines; plus one asserting the canonical form still parses. Spec's inertness paragraph now states what EXACTLY means.

resolutions.title: Escaped backticks incorrectly hide live markers
resolutions.action: computeCodeRegionMask now counts immediately-preceding backslashes and drops an escaped leading backtick from the candidate run. Reproduced first (a marker between two escaped backticks vanished). Regressions for odd and even backslash counts; the spec's inline-code table gained the row.

resolutions.title: An empty registry file disables the lint without any output
resolutions.action: `sources:` declaring no entries is now a SourceRegistryError naming the file and telling the author to delete it rather than empty it. Reproduced first (sources: {} yielded registryPresent true with zero findings, zero coverage, silent exit 0). The malformed-registry scenario gained the clause; the absent-file-silence test now covers present-but-null AND present-but-empty.

resolutions.title: Schema parameters can traverse outside the schema namespace
resolutions.action: findSchemaFile now requires the kebab SCHEMA_NAME_REGEX and enforces resolved-path containment within each tier (realpath, so symlinks cannot escape either). Reproduced first: `schema: ../../schemas/spec-driven` resolved a planted schema OUTSIDE both tiers and emitted 777. Regression covers four spellings; the spec states the identifier-not-path rule and gains a scenario.

resolutions.title: Tracked markdown read failures are silently reported as scanned
resolutions.action: A tracked path with no working-tree file is still skipped silently (a deleted file is legitimately still tracked), but every OTHER read failure is now a marker-kind finding naming the file, and filesScanned counts files actually READ. Three regressions: non-ASCII name, deleted file, unreadable file (chmod 000) with a stale sibling proving the rest still lints.

resolutions.title: Unmatched backtick runs cause repeated whole-suffix scans
resolutions.action: Pairing is now linear: each run's next equal-length partner is pre-indexed in one backward sweep, replacing the per-unmatched-run re-scan of the remaining group. Regression drives 400 unmatched runs of 17 distinct lengths under a time bound and still finds the live span.

resolutions.title: Prototype properties bypass the closed engine-source membership check
resolutions.action: Object.hasOwn replaces the `in` operator. Reproduced first: `engine: toString` threw `TypeError: definition.params is not iterable` instead of the clean unknown-source error. Regression covers toString, constructor and hasOwnProperty, asserting the error lists the four exposed names.

resolutions.title: The four motivating fixtures do not exercise the lint implementation
resolutions.action: MERGED with the fresh pass's identical finding (review-system-2026-09-17T20-53-54Z, correctness/WARNING at :33). The three numeric defects now run through runSourceLint in a real git fixture and assert the discriminated mismatch record; the compound case runs through parseMarkedSpans plus a newly-exported checkSpanAgainstValue — the one comparison the CLOSED v1 table cannot produce as a source value — so it touches the product rather than String.prototype. An agreeing span of the same shape is asserted too, so the four failures mean something.

resolutions.title: Use NUL-delimited git output for the project file domain
resolutions.action: MERGED with the fresh pass's CRITICAL at the same line (silent non-ASCII domain drop). resolveFileDomain now runs `git ls-files -z -- '*.md'`, splits on NUL and never trims paths. Reproduced the fresh pass's case first (a tracked dé-café.md with a stale span produced no finding, no warning, no coverage). Regressions: non-ASCII name and a path with surrounding spaces.

resolutions.title: The live ruling-count test derives its oracle from the same raw-text assumptions
resolutions.action: The live test now PINS the contract value (10) as task 1.1 asked, and keeps the hand-scan as a second independent witness that must agree. A shared section/fence/bold mistake can no longer pass both sides.

delegation_directive: let's just go ahead and apply the fixes
final_assessment: Half one of the SYSTEM-mode blind pair. 12 of 13 resolved; external C1 (the orbit-architecture-engine opacity contract being false of the shipped parser API) DEFERRED by explicit user ratification — verified real before deferring, and left because its fix is a spec redesign that routes back to explore under R-crc-6 rather than being invented inside a walk. Both CRITICALs from this half were genuine engine defects: one deferred, one (the ruling parse reading a second fence grammar) repaired by importing the shared tracker, with the engine-wide parser unification recorded as a declared residual. Three decision-lane calls were settled under R-crc-3 and applied under the user's blanket directive; the other nine were obvious fixes previewed at triage. 2197 tests green; validate --all --strict clean; the no-registry path re-verified byte-identical against the pre-change HEAD build.
